payload.text: **`intent explore` OPENS THE TUI AT THE TOP OF THE MODEL, AND IT IS THE SAME VIEW STACK ENTERED AT A DIFFERENT DEPTH RATHER THAN A SECOND SURFACE.** (hv requirement 2026-08-30, added while AFK; scoped by ic, minted by vc.) `explore` enters at ENTITIES; `intent edit <kind> <id>` enters the same stack at ITEM. Same keys, same menu, same descents -- **so a second navigation model is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.** **THE VERB IS `explore` AND NOT `browse` ON THE DESIGN'S OWN GROUNDS, NOT ON TASTE: `intent browse <kind> <id>` already ships meaning OPEN IN THE BROWSER**, and one word carrying two meanings is the exact defect `tui-design.md` section 5 records for `Up`/`Down` and section 4 for `/`-as-menu-and-prefix. **`explore` TAKES AN OPTIONAL ADDRESS** (hv, 2026-08-30, overruling vc; recorded by ic at `d9860add`). hv's words: _I see no reason why `intent expl[ore] ...` couldn't take an intent://... URL scheme URI or even an ID that it tries to match to something if it can, and if it can't it just opens at the root. That doesn't obviate `intent edit ...` in any way._ **THE RULING THIS REPLACES SAID THE OPPOSITE AND IT IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, BECAUSE THE REASON IT DID NOT REACH IS THE USEFUL PART.** vc's objection was three doors onto one surface, and its whole content was NO SECOND RESOLVER -- which this does not create: `address::promote` for a bare id (the estate's one door, which refuses ambiguity by naming both forms), `address::parse` for a URI, `View::parse` for a path. **Nothing new resolves anything, so the objection had no subject** (ic, 2026-08-30). Withdrawn, not narrowed. **THE FALLBACK IS THE ROOT PLUS THE REASON ON SCREEN, NEVER THE ROOT IN SILENCE.** hv's _just opens at the root_ contrasts with REFUSING, not with TELLING -- and a fallback that does not announce itself is the answers-confidently-from-partial-evidence class this rewrite exists to remove. `intent edit ST9999` must still refuse, because it was asked to ACT on a specific thing while `explore` was asked to OPEN THE EXPLORER near one. **AND THERE ARE THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO -- THE ADDRESS GRAMMAR IS WIDER THAN THE VIEW LADDER** (ic's finding, ruled into this row by vc 2026-08-30). `Entity` carries `Node`, `NodeInbox`, `Event`, `At` and `Attachment`: all addressable, none with a view. So *named nothing* and *named something this surface cannot show* are DIFFERENT FACTS and must read differently -- telling an operator that `intent:///nodes/vc` named nothing is FALSE, and it is the shape that sends them hunting for a thing they already have. **Same family as clap's `unrecognized subcommand` on an ambiguous prefix: a gate that cannot say WHICH of two things went wrong eventually says the one that starts a search instead of ending it.** **AND A FIFTH INPUT CASE THAT WAS IN NEITHER LIST, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED: `ST9999`.** `promote` is purely syntactic and never reads the store, so a well-formed id for an ABSENT thread resolves perfectly; `rows_for` renders a form that will not load with its field names intact; **so an absent thread and an empty one PAINT THE SAME SCREEN.** That is `AC-17.7`'s reachable-and-blank defect arriving through the front door of the feature built after it. The presence test is an INJECTED closure and `the_presence_test_is_actually_consulted` is the control for the whole file -- a `land` that ignored its argument would pass every other assertion in it. **`Landing` LIVES IN `intentsvcs::nav`, BESIDE `View::parse`** (radius ruled by vc): the web face needs the same resolution for a URL bar and a jump-to box, and `intentd` cannot reach the CLI. **THE CHECKABLE PROPERTY, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS A CRITERION AND NOT A TICKET: THE TUI'S VIEW STACK AND THE WEB'S URL PATH ARE THE SAME SEQUENCE, BOTH DERIVED FROM THE SAME SCHEMA RELATIONS, SO NEITHER RENDERER INVENTS A LEVEL.** `[entities]` and `/`; `[entities, thread]` and `/thread`; `[entities, thread, ST0056]` and `/thread/ST0056`. **That is `AC-17.1` one level up -- 17.1 diffs the MODEL after an edit, this diffs the NAVIGATION -- and it is what gives `--browser` an exact meaning at any depth.** Asserted by round-tripping EVERY view the real declaration can produce through its path, never over hand-picked examples. **AND EVERY PATH SEGMENT IS A NAME THE DECLARATION ALREADY CARRIES** (ic's finding, ruled by vc 2026-08-30): `/thread/ST0056/wps`, never `/threads/ST0056/work-packages`. **A pluralisation rule is a SECOND HOME FOR NAMING** -- it mints strings that appear in no declaration, it breaks on the first kind that does not take `-s`, and it must be inverted to route. Section 9 shows a plural in prose and **the prose is what needs correcting, which is hv's hand and is flagged rather than done.** If the web face wants plurals for display, that is a rendering concern layered on ONE derived path, never a second derivation -- **because the moment the two faces derive their own, they are no longer the same sequence and this criterion is unsatisfiable by construction.**
